capabilities: Transcribe speech offline through a locally spawned sherpa-onnx WebSocket server
Insert transcriptions at the cursor or copy them to the clipboard
Select among SenseVoice, FunASR, Paraformer and Qwen3-ASR models and manage the service lifecycle
Build a pinyin lexicon to detect and one-click-correct homophone transcription errors
Control recording, cursor movement and candidate picking with a gamepad
extras: Desktop only (spawns a local subprocess and captures the microphone); requires downloading a server binary and model folders from 230 MB to 3.7 GB; the lexicon and fuzzy matching only affect Chinese text; macOS may block the unsigned binary due to a quarantine flag; recording is capped at 280 seconds; push-to-talk semantics are approximated because Obsidian hotkeys deliver only key-down events.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in speech-to-text, and cloud dictation services require API keys or send audio off the device.

relations.evidence: Offline speech recognition in Obsidian, powered by a locally deployed sherpa-onnx service

requires.name: sherpa-onnx-offline-websocket-server binary and an ASR model folder

summary: Offline speech-to-text dictation that runs a local sherpa-onnx WebSocket service and inserts transcriptions at the cursor via a hotkey.
